en: The Philippines consists of 7,641 islands, making it one of the largest archipelagos in the world.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from north to south.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of approximately 911 square kilometers.
The Philippine Trench is the deepest oceanic trench in the country, reaching a maximum depth of 10,540 meters.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an underground river that flows for 8.2 kilometers directly into the sea.
Palawan is the largest island province in the Philippines, covering a total land area of 14,649 square kilometers.
The Philippines has over 52,000 described species, with more than half of them found nowhere else on Earth.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of about 4,000 millimeters, making it one of the wettest cities.
The Philippines contains 24 active volcanoes, all of which are located along the Pacific Ring of Fire.
The Tabon Caves complex in Palawan consists of at least 200 known caves and shelters spread across 155 hectares.
The Philippine archipelago stretches approximately 1,850 kilometers from north to south across the western Pacific Ocean.
